Article 4
(1) The Regent through regional apparatus establishes a public service work unit that functions as an Integrated Service Center (PPT).
(2) The Integrated Service Center (PPT) as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for women's empowerment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

Article 13
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence include medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is in the form of services and assistance to help victims go through the legal and judicial process.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is in the form of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER III
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 12
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.
(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of West Bangka Regency whether committed in West Bangka or outside West Bangka.
(3) Protection for women and children victims of violence in addition to being provided to residents of West Bangka as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of West Bangka for acts committed within the territory of West Bangka Regency.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal human rights and dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the basic rights of women and children and the best interests of victims.

Article 3
The Cooperation in the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women from gender-based violence and the best interests of children occurring in households or public spaces.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Government of West Bangka Regency.
2. Bupati is the Bupati of West Bangka.
3. Regional Apparatus of the Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head in the administration of regional government consisting of the Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies and Regional Technical Institutions.
4. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among protection providers in delivering services to victims of domestic violence.
5. Protection Administration is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
11. Economic violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
12. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical care (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other Community Organizations.
18. Population is Indonesian citizens and foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for victims of acts of violence is carried out by government agencies, regional governments and social institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities to implement protection.

3.2.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the only police-related provision is Pasal 6(a): "ruang pelayanan khusus di jajaran kepolisian" (special service rooms within the police). This describes a facility/room, not the establishment of a specialised police unit (unit layanan khusus/UPPA, etc.) within police offices. Other articles define protection as possibly carried out by police (Pasal 1(14)) and mention cooperation with police (Pasal 10(a)), but none establishes a dedicated police service unit. The judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to be based on over-interpreting ‘special service rooms’ as a ‘specialised unit’.

3.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy references cooperation with police to report and process perpetrators and notes that handling mechanisms will be stipulated by Regent Regulation, it does not itself provide a concrete mechanism/service (e.g., hotline, complaint desk, reporting channel) for receiving reports or complaints.

3.3.rationale: The Indonesian text does not set out any reporting channel/hotline/complaint desk. Pasal 10(a) only says certain actors may cooperate with police "untuk melaporkan dan memproses" perpetrators, which is not a victim-facing reporting mechanism/service. Pasal 7(2) explicitly defers the handling/service mechanism to a future Regent Regulation (Peraturan Bupati), and the Perda itself provides no concrete reporting mechanism. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ matches the source; the golden ‘Yes’ likely treats generic ‘report to police’ language or deferred mechanisms as equivalent to an actual hotline/reporting service.
